hed: Poland scrambles jets after Yahodyn near-border drones; NATO Rutte cites Putin ‘desperation’
dek: After Sunday’s Russian drone strike on a passenger locomotive at Yahodyn about 2 km from Poland, Polish forces on Monday recovered a suspected Russian drone from the Baltic near Jarosławiec and overnight into Tuesday scrambled jets as a preventive measure amid continued Russian air activity over western Ukraine. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte had called the near-border strikes a sign of Vladimir Putin’s “desperation.” No casualties were reported in the Yahodyn train hit.
alt: Dorohusk railway station on the Polish side of the Ukraine–Poland rail crossing
caption: Dorohusk railway station in Poland, opposite Ukraine’s Yahodyn crossing. File photograph used for layout; not from Sunday’s strike.
byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: CNN’s Monday NATO-edge analysis, the BBC’s Yahodyn write-through, and Euronews’s Poland–Ukraine reaction cast the locomotive strike — and a same-day hit near the Yahodyn–Dorohusk road crossing — as Putin’s terror “knocking” on the EU/NATO door: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha urged denser sanctions, NATO’s Mark Rutte pledged more support for Kyiv after calling the strikes reckless fear-sowing, and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that intensified Russian action could spill toward Polish territory.

cr.body: The New York Post’s Monday Rutte wrap, The Hill’s AP wire, and Al Arabiya’s AFP pickup of the Russian Defense Ministry line present Moscow’s claim that western-Ukraine railway infrastructure is used to move European military cargo — not a VIP assassination plot — while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday that Russian forces operate “across the entire territory of Ukraine” and will continue to do so, framing the episode as logistics warfare near a dual-use border corridor rather than a new NATO Article 5 trigger.
